title: All-Hands: December 2026 - Leadership Update
summary: Quarterly leadership update covering Q4 results, product milestones (Private GA, Dedicated expansion, Optimize improvements), hiring and org priorities, and Q1 objectives. Leadership reviewed ARR and runway briefly, announced customer wins and a few GTM initiatives. Q&A covered security/compliance asks and roadmap timing. Next steps include a follow-up tech deep dive and distributing the leadership deck and intra-company FAQ.
topics: Product milestones: Private GA, Dedicated expansion, Redwood Optimize
next_steps: Share leadership deck and FAQ (Maya to post links by EOD)
Schedule technical deep dive on Private GA for customers (Samir)
CS/Marketing to prepare two customer case studies (Leah)
People to finalize Q1 hiring plan and post roles (Ana)
action_items: Maya Patel - Post slides + infra FAQ to #announcements by 2026-12-15
Samir Kapoor - Organize Private GA tech deep dive and invite list by 2026-12-22
Leah Wong - Draft two customer case studies and share outline by 2026-12-31
Ana Rivera - Publish Q1 hiring priorities and interview panel schedule by 2027-01-07
transcript:
[00:00] Chris Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, let's get started. Quick note - recording is on. We'll run about 50 minutes, and then open Q&A.
[00:28] Maya Patel: Hi all, quick housekeeping, deck is in the chat, link is bit.ly/rw-dec-2026, if you need alt formats ping me.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: I'll kick off with product highlights really quick. Q4 we shipped Private GA, small-batch rollouts to early customers, and the Dedicated expansion - more regions live in eu-west-2 and ap-south-1.
[01:12] Chris Thompson: Great. High level on business: ARR up 34% q/q for the quarter, bookings beat plan by ~6%, and churn is flat. We're seeing good adoption in mid-market.
[01:40] Chris Thompson: A couple of caveats - bookings skewed to a few enterprise deals, so pipeline is still a focus. Also margin compression on some hosted usage due to increased seq lengths on a handful of customers.
[02:05] Samir Kapoor: On infra: Private GA is running on customers' VPCs, we've tightened the KMS path and added HSM integrations for two pilot accounts. We also pushed a kernel selector update that shaves ~8-12% off long-seq latency for some models.
[02:42] Maya Patel: Worth calling out an ops note - we saw a KV cash bug (transcript: kv cash) in one early deployment that caused some cache misses; that's fixed and we added a test. Sorry, kv cache, my bad.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: On Redwood Optimize - the recommendations engine now suggests quantization profiles per workload and has an autosuggest for batching policy. Internal testing shows up to 25% cost reduction without measurable quality regressions on our test prompts.
[03:36] Leah Wong: Customer wins: closed three mid-market PLG expansion deals, and we brought one large enterprise to pilot Redwood Private - big win for the security narrative.
[04:01] Audience: applause / clapping sounds
[04:10] Chris Thompson: Thanks Leah - on go-to-market, we're pivoting to a more reference-driven motion. Expect a push on case studies early next quarter.
[04:30] Ana Rivera: People update - hiring remains open for ICs in infra and product, we're prioritizing security hires and platform SREs. No broad hiring freeze, but we are being selective.
[04:55] Chris Thompson: Financial short note - cash runway remains healthy, we're extending headcount into early next year but with prioritization. We're not doing any sudden cuts.
[05:20] Jordan Lee: Roadmap highlights coming up: Q1 priorities are scaling Dedicated autoscaler, improving cold-starts for large KV caches, and expanding model catalog with two new quantized variants.
[05:45] Maya Patel: On reliability: new tracing hooks are live in prod console. You can now trace request-level latency back to kernel selection and batching windows - this will help debug customer perf issues faster.
[06:10] Samir Kapoor: We're also launching a small internal beta for continuous batching telemetry so SEs can tune batching windows per customer without code changes.
[06:35] Chris Thompson: Security - SOC 2 Type 2 audit in progress, ISO paperwork submitted for a couple of EU prospects. We also added an audit log pipeline to the Private control plane.
[06:58] Audience: murmur, questions starting to come in in chat
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Quick note on pricing - no immediate changes. We're experimenting with a burst add-on for Dedicated customers to allow controlled overage without changing base pricing.
[07:30] Leah Wong: Sales enablement - new playbooks are up in the repo, and the solutions team will run enablement sessions next week.
[07:51] Audience Question (Slack): Is Private GA supported for on-prem air-gapped?
[08:00] Samir Kapoor: Short answer: yes with our on-prem package, but it's a separate onboarding track - talk to SEs to scope network/ops requirements.
[08:20] Audience Question: Any updates on SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[08:30] Maya Patel: We're shipping SCIM by end of month, SAML improvements in January - still working on role mapping and RBAC details.
[08:46] Audience: some cross talk, "will this impact existing customers?"
[09:00] Chris Thompson: No major disruption plan. If needed we'll do rolling updates with canaries.
[09:15] Jordan Lee: A quick product demo clip - (note: a short video was played, not transcribed)
[09:30] Chris Thompson: All right - now I'll share a couple of context items on strategy. First, thesis hasn't changed: winners are those who can make inference predictable and economical. We're doubling down on serving and observability.
[09:55] Chris Thompson: Second, we need to be relentless on unit economics. That means tooling (Optimize), smart routing, and better prefix/KV caching.
[10:20] Maya Patel: From an engineering perspective, prioritizing kernel selection work and continuous batching gives us the best leverage on cost/latency tradeoffs.
[10:40] Samir Kapoor: Ops note - we're standardizing performance benchmarks across regions to avoid the "works here but not there" problem. That will be in CI soon.
[11:05] Audience Question: Can we get more visibility into token-level cost per customer?
[11:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, Console will get token-level breakdowns next sprint; early view will roll out to AE/SEs first.
[11:30] Audience Question: Competitor talk - how do we differentiate vs Anthropic and the big cloud incumbents?
[11:42] Chris Thompson: It's about being production-first and flexible - unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and strong telmetry/rollouts. Not about raw model accuracy alone.
[12:05] Maya Patel: Also, quantization and compiler improvements are a big moat for cost.
[12:25] Chris Thompson: OK, let's move to team highlights - short shoutouts, and then Q&A.
[12:40] Team Shoutouts: Leah thanks AE team, Samir calls out infra on on-call improvements, Maya highlights product interns.
[13:10] Chris Thompson: Now open Q&A. Please use the mic or chat.
[13:24] Audience Member (Speaker 1): Hi, curious about the timeline for the Dedicated autoscaler - when's the beta?
[13:30] Samir Kapoor: Beta next month, limited to customers in eu-west-2 and us-west-2; broader rollout in early Q1.
[13:45] Audience Member: Any performance regressions with the new kernel selector?
[13:50] Maya Patel: We had a couple of edge cases - long-tail sequence patterns caused slightly higher mem usage; fixed in patch 1.2.3.
[14:10] Audience Member: Do we have a public benchmark for Redwood Optimize?
[14:18] Jordan Lee: Not public yet; we'll share internal benchmarks with AE/SE and then a public blog early next quarter.
[14:35] Audience Member: Will the case studies include redaction for PII?
[14:40] Leah Wong: Yes, standard practice - we'll get customer sign-off and redact where needed.
[15:00] Audience Question: Is there a plan for edge deployments?
[15:08] Maya Patel: Edge is on the roadmap, but capacity and consistency issues make it lower priority compared to Private and Dedicated expansion.
[15:30] Chris Thompson: Closing notes - thank you all. Big thanks to infra and product for shipping Private. Quick reminder: share feedback on the leadership doc in the thread.
[15:50] Chris Thompson: We'll follow up with a company FAQ, and SEs will get invites for the tech deep dives.
[16:10] Audience: some final claps, meeting closing
[16:25] End of recording."
